research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current GOV.UK/MHCLG and Planning Inspectorate material checked on 25 July 2026. Full/outline permission, reserved matters, conditions, section 73 changes, non-material amendments, lawful development certificates, permitted development, prior approval, enforcement and appeal procedures remain at their published legal and procedural scope. They are not parcel-specific planning permissions, implementation evidence, immunity from enforcement or Future Growth score accuracy.

source_facts.fact: GOV.UK distinguishes full permission, outline permission, reserved matters, discharge of conditions, amendments, lawful development certificates and prior approvals as different application types.
source_facts.gate: An application type or submission is not a grant of permission or proof of implementation.

source_facts.fact: Permitted development rights are a national grant of planning permission subject to conditions and limitations; some rights require prior approval only on specified matters.
source_facts.gate: PDR availability and prior approval must not be conflated with full planning permission or other consents.

source_facts.fact: Section 191 and 192 certificates determine lawfulness for the described existing or proposed use/development and do not replace compliance with unrelated conditions or other regimes.
source_facts.gate: An LDC is not a fresh discretionary planning permission or universal consent.

source_facts.fact: A breach of planning control includes development without required permission or failure to comply with a planning condition/limitation; enforcement action remains discretionary and fact-specific.
source_facts.gate: A suspected breach, complaint or enforcement notice must not be converted into a final planning merits conclusion.

source_facts.fact: Applications submitted on or after 1 April 2026 use the new procedural guide; standard, major and EIA determination periods and appeal deadlines vary by case type.
source_facts.gate: National appeal timetables are procedural and do not predict appeal success.

source_facts.fact: January-March 2026 district authorities decided 68,400 applications and granted 59,400, an 87% national grant rate.
source_facts.gate: National grant rates must never be used as parcel or project approval probabilities.

official_measurement_examples.name: Q1 2026 national planning decisions
official_measurement_examples.fact: 68,400 district-level applications decided; 59,400 granted; national grant rate 87%.

official_measurement_examples.name: Q1 2026 prior-approval applications
official_measurement_examples.fact: 5,200 reported PDR applications: 2,700 prior approval not required, 1,500 granted and 1,000 refused; reported acceptance 81%.

official_measurement_examples.name: Post-April-2026 standard determination period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current appeal guidance states standard valid planning applications normally have an 8-week LPA determination period unless extended in writing.

official_measurement_examples.name: Post-April-2026 major determination period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current appeal guidance states major valid applications normally have a 13-week determination period unless extended in writing.

official_measurement_examples.name: EIA determination period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current appeal guidance states valid EIA applications normally have a 16-week determination period unless extended in writing.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permitted-development semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK describes PDR as a national grant of planning permission subject to conditions and limitations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Prior-approval scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Prior approval allows the LPA to consider only the specified matters for the relevant PDR class.

official_measurement_examples.name: Enforcement appeal digital route
official_measurement_examples.fact: From 1 June 2026 paper enforcement appeal forms are no longer accepted and appeals use the digital Appeal a Planning Decision service.

core_rules: application submitted is not planning permission granted
application validated is not planning permission granted
full planning permission and outline permission must remain distinct
outline permission does not approve every reserved matter
reserved-matters approval is limited to matters reserved by the outline permission
reserved-matters application is not a new unconditional full permission
discharge-of-condition application is not evidence the condition has been discharged
condition discharge for one condition does not discharge other conditions
pre-commencement condition must not be treated as satisfied without written evidence
planning permission subject to conditions is not evidence conditions have been complied with
section 73 variation is not a free-standing re-consideration of every planning matter
section 73 approval does not erase unaffected conditions or obligations
non-material amendment is not a material amendment permission
non-material amendment application is not approval
lawful development certificate is not discretionary planning permission
existing-use LDC is date-specific to the state of affairs described
proposed-use LDC can be affected by material legal change before development begins
LDC does not remove unrelated planning conditions except as specifically described
PDR is subject to conditions limitations and exclusions
PDR availability must be checked against Article 4 and protected-area restrictions
prior approval is not the same as full planning permission
prior approval scope is limited to specified matters in the relevant PDR class
prior approval not required is not a general certificate that all other consents are satisfied
PDR does not override building regulations listed-building or environmental consents
national PDR acceptance statistics are not project probabilities
national planning grant rates are not parcel approval probabilities
determination time limit is not a promise of approval
expiry of a determination period may create appeal rights and does not automatically grant permission unless the specific regime says otherwise
planning appeal submitted is not appeal allowed
appeal acceptance is not planning permission
Inspector procedure choice does not predict appeal outcome
historic appeal procedure must not override the post-1-April-2026 guide for later applications
pre-April and post-April 2026 procedural guides must remain date-scoped
enforcement complaint is not an enforcement notice
suspected breach is not a final breach determination
enforcement notice is not a final merits judgment after all appeal rights
enforcement action is discretionary and must not be inferred solely from a breach allegation
failure to comply with a planning condition can constitute breach of planning control
permitted-development condition breach can be enforceable
enforcement appeal is not an automatic stay or cancellation unless the law provides it for that case
retrospective planning application is not evidence unlawful development has become lawful
section 62A eligibility depends on current designation and application type
Consultation Direction referral is not Secretary of State call-in or final decision
application fee paid is not planning permission
planning register entry is not evidence of current permission implementation
other regulatory consents remain separate from planning permission
NO_DATA must not be converted into no planning restriction or no enforcement risk
no parcel planning status implementation status or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
